# Nonregular finite-contact buffered dual, volume transport, and log flux

This extends the conservative co-moving-normal construction in Section 7
of `candidate 4f875cf42fc6ba0a`
to finite contact sets and atomic covering rows. It removes cap regularity
and singleton contacts from the SAME-separator volume/log-flux calculation,
under the explicit actual continuation and physical-cone hypotheses below.
It proves no numerical Gamma payment and does not identify volume and
surface couplings.

The regular-singleton flux identities being extended are in
`candidate 8f0725a173821a00`.
The nonregular inverse and finite-contact continuation, uniform signed
energy envelope, and actual atomic hinge are separate audited inputs.

## 1. Actual hypotheses and all retained derivatives

Let C be a compact canonical finite positive-fiber hull with mixed measure
dm, total mass M, continuous dimension d, N=d+1, and within-fiber
covariance Sigma. Set Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u). The parameter

    L(w)=min_r A_r(w)>0

is finite-PL concave with a positive extension to a fixed neighborhood and
M^(-1) integral log L dm=0. The actual buffer is

    f(z,y)=[L(z,y) E_(K_z)(y)/M]^(1/N).

Assume an attained unpenalized joint local minimum beta=Q/M and a finite
covering construction as follows. Each proper group i has mass-Q caps
H_ij={N_ij.w>=c_ij}, with nonzero continuous normals u_ij, normalized
Gamma(u_ij)=1, and positive rho_ij summing to one. Its old zero contact
set is a FINITE set of proper deepest marks

    Y_ia=(p_ia,y_ia),             a in A_i.

There is one such mark per assigned base; a mark can occur in several
groups. The actual full contact-minimum cover, nearby quantiles, and
strict gaps outside the old deepest set are available. Atomic groups are
fixed pure-base mass-Q caps covering the remaining deepest bases. Assume
their compressed count m_A satisfies beta m_A<1.

The admissible body/parameter tests form a cone stable under finite
addition of ACTUAL paths. Body paths have bounded signed radial first
speeds v and the proved uniform shape envelope near the finitely many
marks. Parameter directions h satisfy h+cL concave on a common
neighborhood for some c>=0. In particular allow both signs of affine
functions, both signs of L, and h=-Phi for every finite convex maximum of
affine functions. These give actual simultaneous perturbations on nearby
bodies. The cone also contains the actual summed atomic hinge action.
These are physical premises, not inferred from formal independent jets.

Define the old linear functionals

    D=integral_boundary v,
    C_ia=integral_boundary(K_pia) P_ia(X)^(-N) v,
    P_ia(X)=1+a_ia.(X-y_ia),
    J_i=integral_boundary sum_j rho_ij[u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2 v,
    s(v)=M^(-1) integral_boundary log L v,
    H(h)=M^(-1) integral_S h/L dm,

where a_ia is the ordinary ENERGY normalizer and E_ia=E_(K_pia)(y_ia).
Write f_ia=f(Y_ia), L_ia=L(Y_ia), and

    K_ia=C_ia/(N E_ia)+J_i/(2M)-(N+2)D/(2NM)
                  -s(v)/N-h(Y_ia)/(N L_ia)+H(h)/N.     (1)

Every mass, covariance, energy, and full-space log normalization term is
retained in (1). No derivative of a reoptimized parameter is assumed.

Allow the cap normal N_ij to change by nu_ij. These are independent signed
variables for the cap copies, but SHARED across contacts a of a group.
Uniform contact localization gives the exact first contact budget

    alpha_i'=min_a alpha_ia',
    alpha_ia'=sum_j rho_ij nu_ij.Y_ia
       -epsilon f_ia sum_j rho_ij grad Gamma(u_ij).u'_ij
       +epsilon f_ia K_ia.                              (2)

This is the derivative of the exact minimum over the assigned current
sampled fibers. No derivative of the minimizing marks enters. Concavity
and uniqueness in each assigned fiber, plus the uniform first expansion,
justify this finite envelope even if L is not differentiable at a mark.

## 2. Concave lower responses and one dual

On an inside-supporting other fiber, drop its nonnegative loss hinge but
KEEP its full-fiber body loss. Keep outside hinges exactly. In the notation
of the preceding source this gives

    R_ij^0=B_ij(v)+S_ij r-m_ij.nu_ij
      -integral_outside [(nu_ij.w-r)/b_ij-v(w)]_+ dS,  (3)

where b_ij=||u_ij|| and S_ij>0 is the actual proper coarea. This is jointly
concave, increasing onto R in r, and no larger than the actual loss.
For a prescribed contact budget alpha_ia, equalize its cap losses with
sum_j rho_ij r_j=alpha_ia. Denote the resulting conservative loss by
ell_ia. It is jointly concave in the actual direction and the free normal
variables. Monotonicity in the budget and (2) give EXACTLY

    ell_i^0=min_a ell_ia.                               (4)

Thus ell_i^0 is concave and is a lower bound for the actual group loss.
The normalized conservative improvement is ell_i^0-beta D. Atomic
improvements are their actual full-fiber cap loss minus beta D.
Simultaneous positivity would be an actual strict descent via the given
cover, so the common hypograph separation supplies one dual.

More explicitly, let b denote an outside-selector tuple in the compact
moment set of the facets. Its coareas T_ijb>0 and loss forms give

    B_ib=sum_j rho_ij/T_ijb,
    theta_ijb=(rho_ij/T_ijb)/B_ib.

Each ell_ia is the infimum of the corresponding linear equalized loss
forms, with the SAME alpha_ia in (2). The infimum is attained by the
actual outside signs at its solved thresholds. A dual convex mixture
has weights lambda_iab>=0 and atomic weights eta_A>=0, with total sum
one. Set

    eta_i=sum_ab lambda_iab,
    kappa_ia=sum_b lambda_iab/B_ib,
    kappa_i=sum_a kappa_ia,
    e_ia=epsilon f_ia kappa_ia,
    e_i=sum_a e_ia,
    Delta=sum_ia e_ia.                                  (5)

The kappa weights, NOT the e weights, determine the contact barycenter.

These statements do not require finitely many PL response branches.
For finitely many test directions the facet selector moment images are
compact, their coareas are bounded below by S_ij, and finite-dimensional
separation applies. A common dual for an entire physically addable test
class follows by compactness: parameterize it by cap weights omega_ij,
contact weights kappa_ia, atomic weights, and weighted outside densities
0<=zeta_ij<=omega_ij on the old faces. The equations below are linear in
these variables. They form a weak-star compact set: sum cap and atomic
weights is one, and the coarea equations bound kappa_i by a fixed maximum
coarea times eta_i. Each prescribed physical or parameter inequality is
weak-star closed (its speed is integrable). Every finite subcollection
has the preceding separator; the finite-intersection property gives one
for all tests. No closure of the physical image cone is presumed.

## 3. Effective section weights and the shared contact barycenter

Aggregate the cap weights and outside selectors using lambda_iab theta_ijb:

    omega_ij=sum_ab lambda_iab theta_ijb,
    tau_ij^eff(w)=
        [sum_ab lambda_iab theta_ijb tau_ijb(w)]/omega_ij,
    T_ij=S_ij+integral_outside tau_ij^eff dS/b_ij.

For every group of positive weight all omega_ij>0 and

    omega_ij T_ij=kappa_i rho_ij,
    sum_j omega_ij=eta_i.                               (6)

Inside body/section selectors are respectively 1 and 0; outside body and
section selectors are both tau_ij^eff. The SAME densities determine the
allocated section measure, whose total coarea is T_ij and whose full mean
is denoted bar w_ij.

Testing the shared signed normal variables in the one dual gives

    bar w_ij=Ybar_i-(e_i/kappa_i)(0,grad Gamma(u_ij)),
    Ybar_i=sum_a kappa_ia Y_ia/kappa_i.                 (7)

Indeed their coefficient is rho_ij times
sum_a kappa_ia Y_ia-kappa_i bar w_ij
minus e_i rho_ij times the continuous vector grad Gamma(u_ij).
Both normal signs force it to vanish. Thus

    bar z_ij=sum_a kappa_ia p_ia/kappa_i,
    bar X_ij=sum_a kappa_ia y_ia/kappa_i
                            -(e_i/kappa_i)Sigma u_ij.  (8)

The final equality uses old Gamma(u_ij)=1. No individual-contact section
centroid formula is claimed, and the mean base in (8) need not be integer.

## 4. Atomic rows and SAME-dual volume transport

The dual cannot be atomic-only. If it were, apply the actual summed atomic
hinge: with its standard normalization D=m_A and every selected atomic
cap loss at least one, its weighted improvement is at least
1-beta m_A>0, contradicting the dual. Thus Delta>0 in (5). This uses an
actual member of the SAME physical cone, not a separate parameter stress.

The parameter terms in (1) yield

    sum_ia e_ia h(Y_ia)/L_ia
                      >=(Delta/M) integral_S h/L dm.    (9)

Affine directions of both signs give equal mass and all full first
moments. Negative maxima of affine functions give precisely the tests
needed by the finite-source allocation/separation proof. Consequently
there is an actual martingale from

    mu_V=sum_ia (e_ia/L_ia) delta_Yia
    to dnu_V=(Delta/M) dm/L.                            (10)

Both L moments equal Delta. Repeated occurrences of the same proper mark
can be merged, and then split back in their e_ia proportions. No cap
regularity or choice of a separate parameter-only separator is used.

Concave Jensen equality localizes every positive row to every active
plane of L. Since its target has positive bounded mixed-volume density,
two active planes with different continuous gradients would force that
row into a mixed-null hyperplane. Therefore each source with e_ia>0 has
a UNIQUE continuous gradient c_ia of L. This is proved AFTER (10), not
assumed to define parameter jets or the physical cone.

The old contact tangent relation now becomes

    U_i:=sum_j rho_ij u_ij
       =epsilon f_ia[a_ia+c_ia/(N L_ia)]
                     for every positive contact a.    (11)

Before uniqueness one only uses the appropriate continuous supergradient
at the contact. Equation (11) follows because that fiber-interior mark
minimizes the old affine-minus-concave contact expression. In particular

    kappa_ia U_i=e_ia[a_ia+c_ia/(N L_ia)].             (12)

The exact gradient-labeled volume identities continue to hold:

    (Delta/M) integral chi(c(w))(1,w)/L dm
        =sum_ia (e_ia/L_ia) chi(c_ia)(1,Y_ia),
    (Delta/M) integral chi(c(w)) dm
        =sum_ia e_ia chi(c_ia).                        (13)

These give each label's ORIGINAL mass, and its tilted full first moment.
They do not give an original-volume row barycenter or a surface coupling.

## 5. Physical density and summed force identities

Let W be the cap selector with proper cap weights omega_ij, plus the
atomic whole-fiber selectors weighted by eta_A. Put kappa=Delta/(NM).
The actual body part of the common conservative dual is

    integral_boundary Xi v<=0,

where

    Xi_z(X)=W_z(X)-beta
      +sum_(ia:p_ia=z) e_ia P_ia(X)^(-N)/(N E_ia)
      +(1/(2M))sum_i e_i sum_j rho_ij[u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2
      -(N+2)Delta/(2NM)-kappa log L(z,X).               (14)

All supporting selections in W have been fixed by the SAME dual as
(9). They are not freely chosen closed indicators. The allocated
Gauss--Green rule is valid because inside body+section selectors equal
one and outside body and section selectors agree.

Let S_ij(z) denote these allocated coareas on fiber z. The fiber force is

    F_z=integral_boundary(K_z) Xi_z n_z dS
       =sum_ij omega_ij S_ij(z)u_ij
        -sum_(ia:p_ia=z)e_ia a_ia
        -kappa integral_Kz grad_X log L.                (15)

The following exact identities survive the contact averaging:

    sum_z F_z=0,
    sum_z z tensor F_z=0,
    sum_z integral_boundary(K_z) Xi_z X tensor n_z=0.  (16)

Here is the explicit reason no contact covariance was silently discarded.
By (6)--(8) the cap force and its base moment are

    sum_j omega_ij T_ij u_ij=kappa_i U_i,
    sum_j omega_ij T_ij bar z_ij tensor u_ij
                  =sum_a kappa_ia p_ia tensor U_i.

Applying (12) converts these to the corresponding sums with e_ia and
individual source normalizers. Their extra L-gradient terms cancel
exactly with (13), just as in the singleton proof.

Similarly, the continuous cap-section moment is

    sum_j omega_ij T_ij bar X_ij tensor u_ij
       =sum_a kappa_ia y_ia tensor U_i
                          -e_i Sigma C_i^u,
    C_i^u=sum_j rho_ij u_ij u_ij^T.                   (17)

Use (12) again. The terms of the continuous affine tensor in (16) are

    W-beta: sum_ia e_ia y_ia tensor[a_ia+c_ia/(N L_ia)]
                                      -sum_i e_i Sigma C_i^u,
    energy: Delta Id/N-sum_ia e_ia y_ia tensor a_ia,
    covariance: Delta Id/2+sum_i e_i Sigma C_i^u,
    constant: -(N+2)Delta Id/(2N),
    logarithm: -kappa integral_S X tensor grad_X log L.

The raw Q Id terms cancel because all proper and atomic cap weights sum
to one and every old cap has mass Q. The scalar Id coefficient is zero,
and (13) cancels the remaining logarithmic tensor. This proves (16).

For the ordinary centroid radial array h_z=n_z.(X-g_z), the remaining
response is still

    integral_boundary Xi h=-sum_z g_z.F_z.             (18)

It vanishes for an affine centroid graph; otherwise neither the volume
coupling nor the shared contact average cancels it. That radial array
need not be an actual compatible motion.

## 6. Affine nullity without a nonexistent PL parameter jet

A finite-PL L pulled through a common affine body map may have moving
creases, so -grad L.V need not be a continuous uniform parameter jet.
It must NOT be inserted formally into the cone in Section 1.

Instead compose any actual admissible body/parameter/cap path with the
same lattice-preserving fiber-affine map. Pull L and all planes along
that map. Exact geometric normalization, energy covariance and the
within-fiber covariance norm make its normalized buffered covering
response unchanged. This supplies affine null directions at the ACTUAL
response level, without differentiating a crease. On an old supporting
face the transported margin and body speeds agree, so every inside or
outside hinge is pointwise zero; the conservative inside-zero bound is
exact on this action. The algebraic cancellations (16) were independently
derived after the volume transport established source gradients, so no
circular pre-transport differentiability is involved.

## 7. Exact scope

Other-fiber supporting facets and multiple finite proper contacts do not
prevent this conservative SAME-dual construction. Shared normal controls
give only the averaged section means (7)--(8); their full bookkeeping is
nevertheless sufficient for (13)--(18). Atomic rows remain present and
are excluded from carrying the entire dual only by the actual hinge.

What remains assumed is an attained positive finite-PL parameter, the
proved actual finite-contact cover and uniform local shape expansions,
and an actually addable joint test class. No smoothing approximation,
optimizer derivative, generalized trace-to-uniform conversion, surface/
volume coupling identification, or Gamma payment is inferred. The
companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_nonregular_multicontact_log_flux_defect_transport.py`
passes 813 exact aggregation and tensor checks; it does not manufacture
a fictitious stationary geometric menu.
